It also served to allow grandparents to live close to their children and grandchildren and others important to their quality of life. This type of community fills a distinct need, not only for the aging population within, but to give an important balance and stability to the surrounding area. Anyone who has had a close relationship with an aging relative probably understands the importance of that type of influence. The information found on Zillow and other such sites puts senior-living communities like mine in jeopardy by not taking these factors into consideration by lumping the rents and prices in with the prices outside the senior community. I have observed that home prices within senior communities have more than doubled in just a few years, causing rents and taxes to rise to historic levels, forcing more and more seniors to reluctantly move from the familiarity and security of their homes in search of housing they can afford, often great distances from where they would otherwise choose to live. This is nothing short of disastrous for them, their friends and families, and for society in general. Zillow must consider its role in this devastating situation and do what it takes to remedy it. Not all housing is equal and people who choose to ignore that endanger nothing less than the future of our society. Don't believe me? The next grandmother you see living on the street could be yours!
